purpose: Verify binding cardinality and scope evidence between authorization/approval decisions and tool executions without conflating decision identity, tool-call identity, or external-effect truth.

invariants.rule: decision_id and execution/tool_call identity are distinct namespaces; neither may be inferred from the other.
A per_call decision may bind at most one execution.
A standing decision may bind multiple executions, but each execution must independently carry a scope-binding result.
An execution bound to a deny decision is a contradiction.
scope_binding=not_checked is UNRESOLVED, never upgraded to match.
A PASS validates only decision-to-execution binding evidence; it does not prove the external side effect.

pressure_sources.claim: AITF separates authorization/approval decision identity from Tool Execution ID and records approval scope-binding as match, mismatch, or not_checked.
Devplane marks allow_always/reject_always as standing decisions whose later covered calls may not emit another decision row.
Tracelyt preserves permanent/temporary decision source while correlating individual tool lifecycle events with tool_call_id.

ACP v2 gives each invocation a toolCallId while permission choices distinguish allow_once from standing allow_always/reject_always; command permission subjects allow toolCallId to be unavailable before execution starts.
Agenticos models APPROVE_ALL as standing conversation consent while each gated call still records its own tool_call_id/audit row; one approval mode can therefore cover multiple execution identities.
